sections.h2: Where is St. George, Utah, and how big is it?
sections.html:
St. George sits in the southwest corner of Utah, on the Arizona border, and is the county seat of Washington County. It is on Interstate 15, about 118 miles northeast of Las Vegas and 300 miles south-southwest of Salt Lake City, at an elevation of 2,530 feet.

The city covers roughly 77 square miles in the northeastern edge of the Mojave Desert, just south of the Pine Valley Mountains. The Virgin River and Santa Clara River both run through the valley, and Fort Pearce Wash carries water during storms. Zion National Park lies to the east and Snow Canyon State Park is close to town.

The Census Bureau counted 95,342 residents in 2020 and estimates 108,713 for July 1, 2025. That is a jump of about 13,000 people in five years, which tells you how many houses have gone up in recent years.

sections.h2: What is the history of St. George?
sections.html:
St. George began in 1861 as a cotton mission. About 300 families were called to settle the area at the church conference of October 6, 1861, under apostle Erastus Snow. The city was named for apostle George A. Smith and was incorporated on January 17, 1862.

Cotton never paid off, but the nickname "Utah's Dixie" stuck. The St. George Utah Temple was finished in April 1877 and is the oldest temple in the church still in use. Much of the housing around it is far newer, since the population has roughly doubled since 2000 (49,728 residents then, 95,342 in 2020).

The valley has had its share of natural events. A 1992 earthquake caused about $1 million in damage and destroyed three houses. In January 2005 a regional flood killed one person and destroyed 28 homes along the Santa Clara River. Both are reminders to check a property's flood and soil history before you set a price.

sections.h2: What does the St. George economy rely on?
sections.html:
The St. George economy leans on tourism, manufacturing and new-home construction. More than a dozen golf courses stay open year-round, and the city is a well-known retirement destination.

  • SkyWest Airlines is headquartered in St. George.
  • The Washington County School District has its main offices here.
  • St. George Regional Hospital, an Intermountain facility, is the only 24-hour trauma center between Las Vegas and the Wasatch Front.
  • Utah Tech University had 12,567 students in 2023 to 2024, and Dixie Technical College, Rocky Vista University College of Osteopathic Medicine and a Utah State University campus are also in town.

Big events bring crowds, including the St. George Marathon, the Ironman triathlon and the Huntsman World Senior Games. A house near a venue or a course can draw visitors, but it can also bring traffic and noise that buyers weigh.

sections.h2: How does the desert climate affect a St. George house?
sections.html:
St. George has long, hot summers, and that heat is the main thing a buyer inspects. Average monthly temperatures run from 42.1 degrees in December to 87.8 degrees in July, and about 60 afternoons a year reach 100 degrees or higher. The record is 118 degrees, set on July 4, 2007, the hottest reading ever logged in Utah.

The city gets about 9 inches of precipitation a year and an average of 1.4 inches of snow. Roughly 60 mornings drop to freezing or below, so pipes in poorly insulated homes can still be a concern.

  • Air conditioners and roofs take the most wear, so their age tends to matter in an inspection.
  • Sun-baked stucco, window seals and flat roofs can show damage that is easy to miss from the street.
  • Homes near the Santa Clara River or a wash carry the flood history of the 2005 event, so ask about drainage.

sections.h2: Which water rules shape St. George homes and yards?
sections.html:
Water supply is a live issue in Washington County. In 2022 the Washington County Water Conservancy District announced an ordinance that bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial, institutional and industrial developments and limits grass at new homes.

Each city in the county enforces the rules, including water-waste complaints, metering data and penalties. An added fee for heavy water use began in 2023, and the money pays for rebates to replace grass with water-efficient landscaping. The district projected savings of nearly 11 billion gallons over ten years.

If your yard has a large lawn, ask the city or your water provider what applies before you spend money on landscaping to sell.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and roads should a St. George seller know?
sections.html:
St. George is made up of named areas that buyers recognize, and each has a different feel. Wikipedia lists Downtown, Bloomington, Entrada, Green Valley, Little Valley, Red Cliffs, Snow Canyon, Sunbrook, Sunriver, The Ledges, Tonaquint and Desert Hills among them.

  • Interstate 15 runs northeast to southwest through the city.
  • State Route 7, the Southern Parkway, runs east and west along the south edge, and SR-8, SR-34 and SR-18 also serve the city.
  • St. George Regional Airport in the southeast has flights on American, Delta and United, all flown by SkyWest.
  • SunTran runs seven fixed bus routes.

Public high schools in the Washington County School District include Desert Hills, Dixie, Pine View, Snow Canyon and Crimson Cliffs. Which one serves the house is often a first question from a family moving in.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a St. George house?
sections.html:
Washington County property taxes are due November 30 each year, even when you do not get a notice. The county treasurer says taxes are a lien on the property, not on a person, so an unpaid bill stays with the house when it sells.

The title company prorates the bill at closing, and your settlement statement shows each side's share. Under Utah Code section 59-2-1331, a payment after the due date is delinquent and carries a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, which falls to 1% if everything is paid by January 31.

  • Treasurer: 111 East Tabernacle St., St. George, (435) 301-7720. Partial payments of $10 or more per parcel are accepted at any time.
  • Auditor: (435) 301-7220. If the county Board of Equalization rules against you, a further appeal goes to the Utah State Tax Commission on Form TC-194, filed with the auditor within 30 days of the decision.
  • Each May the clerk-auditor sells properties that have been delinquent for at least five years.

Utah gives a 45% exemption on a primary residence, up to one acre. Rental homes can qualify, while vacation homes and time-shares do not, so a second home in St. George is taxed on its full value. Ask the Washington County assessor how your parcel is classified.

sections.h2: What do St. George sellers usually face?
sections.html:
St. George has an older population than most Utah cities, with 21.8% of residents age 65 or older and a reputation as a retirement destination. That means downsizing moves and inherited houses are part of the picture here.

The problems sellers describe to us are practical ones: an air conditioner or roof near the end of its life, a yard that costs too much to water, an heir who lives in another state, or a house that is hard to show in July heat.

A cash sale skips the listing prep. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to repair the roof, replace the AC or stage the yard. You can compare that against a listing, and an offer does not obligate you to accept.

faqs.q: How many people live in St. George, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 108,713 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 95,342 in the 2020 census. The city is the largest in Washington County and the county seat.

faqs.q: When are St. George property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property taxes in Washington County are due November 30 each year. After that date they are delinquent, and Utah law adds a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, reduced to 1% if paid by January 31.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a St. George house sells?
faqs.a: The title company prorates the bill at closing, so the seller covers the days they owned the house and the buyer covers the rest. The lien follows the property, so any unpaid balance must be settled at or before closing.

faqs.q: Does St. George have special water or landscaping rules?
faqs.a: Yes. A 2022 Washington County Water Conservancy District ordinance limits grass at new homes and bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial and industrial sites. Cities enforce it, and a heavy water-use fee began in 2023. Ask the city how it applies to your lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell a St. George house that needs repairs or has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, including ones with deferred repairs, heat-damaged roofs or tenants in place. Tell us about the house and we will give you an offer you are free to decline.
